results.title: machine learning - What is the best measure for detecting overfitting? - Artificial Intelligence Stack Exchange
results.content: Stack Exchange network consists of 183 Q&A communities including Stack Overflow, the largest, most trusted online community for developers to learn, share their knowledge, and build their careers. And the problem that I face is the lack of a good method to judge if the model overfits before using the test set. I encountered the cases where the model that was good on both training and validation sets, behaved poorly on the test set for both randomized and not randomized training and validation splits. The safest method I've found is to use **cross-validation** for hyperparameter selection **and a hold-out test set** for a final evaluation. The second type of overfitting you need to detect is **on the test set**. In this case (if your model is practically untrainable due to the small size) you can resort to cross-validation, **but you risk overfitting on the validation set** and not having any way to detect it.

results.title: Distinction Between Analysis Types and Experimental Designs - PTB
results.content: What is the difference between all of the types of analysis in ABA, like parametric, non-parametric, component, comparative, functional, and the different types of experimental designs, like reversal, multiple baseline, multielement, changing criterion, and so on. For example, in ABA, in a parametric analysis, the experimental question is what value of the IV will be most effective in a non-parametric analysis. We are asking how behavior is different in treatment versus non-treatment conditions. In a component analysis, we ask which parts or combinations of treatments in a treatment package are effective, or not. In a comparative analysis, we ask which independent treatment is most effective. In a functional analysis, we ask what the function of the behavior is. For a comparative analysis, you could use a multi-element treatment design or a multiple treatment reversal design. results.content:
Title: Moving on from OntoNotes: Coreference Resolution Model Transfer - ADS
## ADS. ## Moving on from OntoNotes: Coreference Resolution Model Transfer. #### Abstract. Academic neural models for coreference resolution (coref) are typically trained on a single dataset, OntoNotes, and model improvements are benchmarked on that same dataset. However, real-world applications of coref depend on the annotation guidelines and the domain of the target dataset, which often differ from those of OntoNotes. We aim to quantify transferability of coref models based on the number of annotated documents available in the target dataset. We examine eleven target datasets and find that continued training is consistently effective and especially beneficial when there are few target documents. We establish new benchmarks across several datasets, including state-of-the-art results on PreCo. :   10.48550/arXiv.2104.08457. :   * Computer Science - Computation and Language.

results.content:
Title: Corpora for English Semantics
A number of large corpora of English text include **semantic annotations**, such as named entities, word senses, predicate-argument structures, and coreference. Note that the verb *answer* has no VerbNet mapping, so it falls back to the PropBank annotation. * Annotates the WSJ corpus (1M words) for verb propositions, applying a lexicon of verb frames to predicates and their arguments in the text. + Mappings from PropBank frame rolesets to VerbNet verb classes/thematic roles are available in: the standalone PropBank release (though with limited coverage); the SemLink 1.1 release; and the PropBank lexicon within OntoNotes. It aims to provide uniform syntactic and semantic annotations for this data, including: named entities, coreference, word senses, PropBank verb propositions, and (eventually) noun propositions. It is important to note that OntoNotes provides both PropBank annotations and OntoNotes sense annotations for verbs, and that these use a different numbering scheme.
